answer: Escrowed deposits and a referral graph stop bulk fakes. Each applicant locks 200 units for 20 epochs and names one sponsor; a dispute slashes both. A canyon of copies shows as a star cluster of shared sponsors that auditors flag. Making 1,000 fakes locks 200,000 units, against about 30,000 units of reward, so it loses money. Honest agents pay one deposit, built on basalt not borrowed names, and earn undiluted rewards as profit hits its nadir.
